corrected_coding_set.short_desc: Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale
Anoxic brain damage, not elsewhere classified
Acute embolism and thrombosis of unspecified deep veins of right lower extremity
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Presence of other vascular implants and grafts (IVC filter)

code_actions.rationale: No documentation of diastolic congestive heart failure; imaging and consults document acute right ventricular dysfunction from PE with preserved LV EF. I50.30 is not supported.
No chart documentation of prior TIA or cerebral infarction; the admitting H&P explicitly states no prior thromboembolic disease, contradicting Z86.73.
Nursing/progress documentation explicitly states no renal replacement was required and AKI was improving; RRT was not performed and this procedure is unsupported.

discharge_disposition: 62 - Discharged/transferred to an inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF)

evidence.quote: Massive bilateral pulmonary artery emboli with saddle embolus at the main pulmonary artery bifurcation.

On EMS arrival the patient was in pulseless ventricular tachycardia. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after 15 minutes of CPR with three defibrillation attempts and multiple rounds of ACLS medications.
Targeted temperature management was initiated for post-arrest neuroprotection.
Neuroprognostication at 72 hours indicated intact function with follow-up expected excellent.
Catheter-directed thrombolysis with tissue plasminogen activator was performed with excellent response and hemodynamic improvement.
Reason for Admission: Massive pulmonary embolism with cardiac arrest requiring post-arrest care and thrombolysis.
BMP: Na 132, K 4.8, Cl 98, CO2 19, BUN 72, creatinine 3.75 mg/dL, glucose 211 mg/dL, Ca 8.1, Mg 2.0, Phos 4.9.
No renal replacement required; AKI improving.
Right ventricular dilation with severe hypokinesis. Left ventricular ejection fraction preserved.
Apixaban 5 mg PO BID PE and DVT
On arrival to the emergency department the patient was intubated with GCS 3 pre-sedation.

The course was complicated by right ventricular failure with rapid recovery, mild post-arrest AKI managed conservatively, and provoked right common femoral DVT identified on subsequent duplex ultrasound requiring IVC filter placement given bleeding concerns from recent thrombolysis.

system_note: Summary of what was billed vs. what the record supports (with citations): - Principal diagnosis billed: I26.99 (position 1). The chart documents massive bilateral pulmonary embolism as the precipitating event with imaging confirmation: CT pulmonary angiography states Massive bilateral pulmonary artery emboli with saddle embolus at the main pulmonary artery bifurcation (Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Pulmonary Angiography, p.206). The Discharge/Transfer Summary lists the Reason for Admission as Massive pulmonary embolism with cardiac arrest requiring post-arrest care and thrombolysis (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1011). These notes support retaining I26.99 and sequencing it as principal (position 1) because the record repeatedly documents massive PE as the acute precipitating condition that required emergent intervention (catheter-directed thrombolysis) (CT Pulmonary Angiography p.206; Discharge / Transfer Summary p.1011; Interventional Cardiology / Interventional Radiology - Emergent p.152). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n13 (p.206); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n1171 (p.1011); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n12 (p.152). - Cardiac arrest (I46.9, MCC) is supported by contemporaneous documentation of pulseless VT, CPR and ROSC: On EMS arrival the patient was in pulseless ventricular tachycardia. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after 15 minutes of CPR with three defibrillation attempts and multiple rounds of ACLS medications (History & Physical (Admitting), p.312). Post-arrest care (TTM, ICU admission) is also documented. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n9 (p.312). Keep I46.9 as a secondary MCC-level code. - Anoxic brain damage (G93.1, MCC) - provider-level documentation and post-arrest neurocare are present: TTM was initiated for post-arrest neuroprotection (History & Physical (Admitting), p.312), neurology performed post-arrest neuroprognostication with planned 72-hour assessment and documented early neurologic exam and follow-up planning (Neurology Consultation, p.79), and the discharge summary documents the post-arrest neurologic course and outcome. The governing policy accepts provider documentation of post-cardiac-arrest brain injury and initiation of TTM/neuroprognostication as validation for G93.1. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n9 (p.312); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n44 (p.79); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n1171 (p.1011). Keep G93.1 (MCC). - Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (J96.01, MCC) is supported: patient was intubated and mechanically ventilated on arrival and ABG/pulse-oximetry show hypoxemia (ABG pH 7.32 / PaCO2 34 / PaO2 65 on 100% FiO2; P/F ratios in early notes consistent with hypoxemia). The policy presumption (intubation attributed to respiratory failure) applies. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n9 (p.312); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n11 (p.821). Keep J96.01 (MCC). - Acute kidney failure (N17.9, CC) is documented and lab-supported (early creatinine elevation to 3.75 mg/dL on the procedure-day labs and the H&P/problem list documents post-arrest AKI, non-dialysis). Discharge summary documents resolved AKI. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n12 (p.152); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n9 (p.312); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n1171 (p.1011). Keep N17.9 (CC). - Right lower-extremity DVT (I82.401, CC) is supported by subsequent duplex and the discharge summary: provoked right common femoral DVT identified on subsequent duplex ultrasound requiring IVC filter placement (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1011). The record documents the DVT as acquired during the encounter (POA=N). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n1171 (p.1011); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n9 (p.312). Keep I82.401 (POA=N, CC). - Hypothyroidism (E03.9) and Major depressive disorder (F32.9, CC) are both in the history/problem list and discharge medications (levothyroxine, escitalopram) indicate active management/continuation during the encounter. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n9 (p.776 / p.312); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n1171 (p.1012). Keep E03.9 (POA=Y) and keep F32.9 (POA=Y, CC). - Long-term use of anticoagulants (Z79.01, POA=N) and presence of IVC filter (Z95.81, POA=N) are supported: no home anticoagulant is recorded on admission home-medication list, anticoagulation (apixaban) was initiated during the stay and discharge meds list apixaban, and the discharge summary documents IVC filter placement during the stay (Transfer / Discharge Summary, p.1011-1012). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n4 (Patient Facesheet, p.5); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n1171 (p.1011-1012). Keep Z79.01 (POA=N) and Z95.81 (POA=N). - Two billed diagnoses lack clinical support / are miscoded and require removal: 1) I50.30 (Unspecified diastolic (congestive) heart failure, billed as MCC) - the objective cardiology imaging and consult consistently document acute right ventricular dilation/dysfunction from massive PE and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (Transthoracic Echocardiogram: Right ventricular dilation with severe hypokinesis. Left ventricular ejection fraction preserved), and the problem list/discharge summary describe right ventricular dysfunction/recovery rather than CHF or diastolic congestive heart failure. There is no provider documentation explicitly diagnosing diastolic congestive heart failure. Therefore I50.30 is not supported and should be removed. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n14 (Diagnostic Imaging Report - Transthoracic Echocardiogram, p.206); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n1171 (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1011). 2) Z86.73 (Personal history of TIA and cerebral infarction, POA=N) - the admitting H&P explicitly documents the patient as otherwise healthy without prior thromboembolic disease (History & Physical (Admitting), p.776), contradicting a history of prior TIA/stroke. There is no other documentation supporting prior cerebrovascular event. Remove Z86.73. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n9 (History & Physical (Admitting), p.776). - One billed procedure is not supported by the record and should be removed: 5A1D80Z (Performance of urinary filtration, prolonged intermittent, less than 6 hours per day). Nursing and progress documentation explicitly state No renal replacement required; AKI improving (Nursing Progress Note - Evening Shift, p.360). The policy for N17.9 presumes RRT would validate higher acuity; here RRT was not performed. Remove 5A1D80Z. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n23 (Nursing Progress Note - Evening Shift, p.360). - Procedures that are supported and retained: endotracheal intubation (0BH17EZ) - documented intubation on arrival (History & Physical (Admitting), p.312); catheter-directed thrombolysis and thrombolytic administration (027Q3ZZ and 3E043GC) - interventional consult and discharge summary document catheter-directed thrombolysis with tPA (Interventional Cardiology / Interventional Radiology - Emergent, p.152; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1011); IVC filter insertion (06H03DZ) - documented in the discharge summary and problem list (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1011); restoration of cardiac rhythm (5A2204Z) - documented defibrillation and ROSC (History & Physical (Admitting), p.312). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n9 (p.312); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n12 (p.152); NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_23.pdf-n1171 (p.1011). Action taken: remove I50.30 and Z86.73 from the diagnosis list; remove 5A1D80Z from the procedure list. All other billed diagnoses and procedures are supported and retained. Citations above identify the specific documentation and the relevant policy criteria (see Cardiac Arrest with ROSC policy, Anoxic Brain Injury policy, Acute Respiratory Failure policy, Acute Kidney Injury policy).
rationale_letter: Re: Clinical Coding Audit - Claim MR_23 Dear Provider, We performed a DRG-level clinical documentation and coding audit for the inpatient stay (admit 09/05/2026, transfer 01/21/2027) for patient Guadalupe Solano. The review compared the billed diagnosis and procedure lines to the medical record and to the applicable DRG validation policies. Finding We find that two billed diagnosis codes and one billed procedure are not supported by the medical record documentation and should be removed from the claim as submitted: - Remove diagnosis I50.30 (Unspecified diastolic (congestive) heart failure). Basis: the cardiology imaging and consultant documentation attribute the acute cardiac dysfunction to right ventricular dilation and hypokinesis from massive pulmonary embolism, with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction; there is no provider-documented diagnosis of diastolic congestive heart failure. Evidence: Transthoracic Echocardiogram: Right ventricular dilation with severe hypokinesis. Left ventricular ejection fraction preserved (Diagnostic Imaging Report - Transthoracic Echocardiogram, p.206). Discharge summary documents resolved right ventricular dysfunction rather than CHF (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1011). - Remove diagnosis Z86.73 (Personal history of transient ischemic attack and cerebral infarction). Basis: the admitting History & Physical documents the patient as "otherwise healthy, without prior thromboembolic disease," and there is no supporting documentation elsewhere in the chart establishing a prior TIA or cerebrovascular infarction. Evidence: History & Physical (Admitting), Past Medical: "Hypothyroidism, depression. Otherwise healthy, without prior thromboembolic disease." (p.776). - Remove procedure 5A1D80Z (Performance of urinary filtration, prolonged intermittent, less than 6 hours per day). Basis: nursing and progress documentation explicitly document that no renal replacement therapy was required and that AKI was improving; there is no record of RRT being performed. Evidence: Nursing Progress Note - Evening Shift: "No renal replacement required; AKI improving." (p.360). Codes retained The remainder of billed diagnoses and procedures are supported by the record and appropriate per the governing policies, including: - I26.99 (Massive pulmonary embolism) - supported by CT pulmonary angiography (CT Pulmonary Angiography, p.206) and by the clinical course and interventional treatment (catheter-directed thrombolysis) (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.1011; Interventional Cardiology note, p.152). - I46.9 (Cardiac arrest) - supported by EMS/ED and ICU documentation of pulseless VT with CPR, defibrillation, and ROSC after 15 minutes (History & Physical, p.312). - G93.1 (Anoxic brain injury) - supported by documentation of post-arrest neuroprotection and neuroprognostication (TTM initiation, neurology consult) consistent with policy criteria (History & Physical, p.312; Neurology Consultation, p.79). - J96.01 (Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) - supported by intubation and ABG/hypoxemia (History & Physical, p.312). - N17.9 (Acute kidney failure), I82.401 (right common femoral DVT), E03.9 (hypothyroidism), F32.9 (depression), Z79.01 (long-term anticoagulant use - POA=N), and Z95.81 (IVC filter) - all supported in the record (admission notes, labs, procedures, and discharge medications/summary). Correction requested Please accept this as notification that the coding for the stay will be adjusted to remove the unsupported items listed above (I50.30, Z86.73, 5A1D80Z). The corrected principal diagnosis sequencing remains I26.99 (massive pulmonary embolism) as principal with the arrest and post-arrest diagnoses retained as secondary codes per the record's stated reason for admission and clinical course. If you disagree with the removal of any code, please provide source documentation or an addendum clarifying: (1) any prior cerebrovascular event to support Z86.73; (2) a documented diagnosis of diastolic congestive heart failure with rationale (e.g., provider assessment explicitly naming I50.30) to support I50.30; or (3) procedure documentation/orders/flowsheet verifying initiation of renal replacement therapy during the stay to support 5A1D80Z. Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team
